subject: NebulaAI — occupancy validation & GPU mix follow-up
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nebula.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@nebula.ai
Date: 2027-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing intake — initial snapshot attached

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on. We're getting close to a sales decision and need a compact validation of the dedicated capacity sizing you recommended in the deck. Attached is a 48h sample of traffic (nebulaai_workload_sample.csv) and a short telemetry snapshot. High-level summary:

- Current product: conversational assistant (mix of short chat turns + longer generative responses).
- Typical prompt length: mean ~85 tokens, 95th ~240, but we occasionally spike to ~600 tokens.
- Typical response length: mean ~350 tokens, p95 ~920.
- Active concurrent sessions (observed steady-state): ~1.2k; peak concurrent sessions observed in a 10min window: ~3.1k.
- Sustained QPS (all traffic): 220 qps; observed short-term peaks up to 420 qps (bursts 3-7 mins).
- KV/cache hit estimated at ~12-18% (depends on session affinity).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 800ms for interactive flows.
- Model: open LLM family (will likely move to a 4-bit quantized variant).

Primary ask: given the attached sample, what conservative reserved GPU mix and number do you recommend for a pilot (8–12 week reserved commitment)? Also: any immediate gaps in the data we should surface to avoid underprovisioning?

Happy to set a 30-min slot for a quick walkthrough.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Head of Platform
NebulaAI

Attachments: nebulaai_workload_sample.csv (CSV, 2.4MB); nebulaai_telemetry_snapshot.json (JSON, 1.1MB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nebula.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-25T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake — initial snapshot attached

Thanks Lisa — got the files and a useful summary. Quick clarifying questions before we sketch an occupancy matrix:

1) Session duration distribution: do you have a CDF or percentiles (median / p75 / p95) for session length? That drives how KV cache amortizes.
2) Are requests predominantly single-turn (stateless) or are you keeping long conversation histories per session?
3) What fraction of traffic requires streaming (token-by-token) vs chunked responses? Streaming reduces batch efficiency.
4) Do you expect to enable 4-bit quantization for the pilot, or will you ship the full-precision variant first?
5) Any hard SLA for p99 or RTO on bursts (e.g., must always meet p99 vs acceptable fallback to smaller model)?

If you can drop a 24h token-histogram or a small sample of RPC traces (headers showing seq length and timing) that'd let us run a quick replay to produce a conservative GPU occupancy table. I'm happy to run that and share a 2-page hypothesis (GPU SKUs, count, expected p95/p99 and unit costs).

Propose a 30-min call today at 2pm PT; if that works I'll book.

Best,
Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pre-sales-intake-form-v2.docx (link)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nebula.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake — initial snapshot attached

Looping in a quick hypothesis from pre-sales sizing playbook (high level) — we can refine after the replay: 

- Baseline hypothesis (conservative, no quantization): aim for a mix that handles 420 qps peak with headroom for bursty 10min windows. For Nebula's prompt/response mix and KV hit ~15% we expect per-GPU effective qps around 45–60 on A100 80GB with optimized kernel + batching.
- Suggested pilot: 6 x A100-80GB (reserved) + 2 x A10g for overflow and cheap parallelism OR 4 x H100 (for headroom on long sequences) depending on model shape.
- If you enable 4-bit quantization and we can accept p99 soft-fallbacks to a cheaper model, a 20–30% reduction in GPUs is plausible.
- Important telemetry we need to validate: per-request token counts (prompt + response), inter-arrival distribution, and session-affinity map.

Operational asks:
- Will Nebula allow a short workload replay (we run a synthetic replay inside Redwood sandbox) under NDA? That gives us an accurate occupancy table.
- If yes, share a sanitized 24h sample and guidance on which routes must maintain p99 SLA.

I'll prepare a quick occupancy matrix and cost delta scenarios if you give the green light for a replay.

—Marissa
Head of Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nebula.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-26T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake — initial snapshot attached

Thanks — answers inline and attaching a cleaned sample.

- Session length percentiles (24h sample): median 12s, p75 20s, p95 82s. Most sessions are short bursts of 1–6 turns.
- Conversation length: typically 3–6 turns; we keep last 6 turns in the context window.
- Streaming: ~70% of responses are streamed token-by-token (interactive UI).
- Quantization: engineering intends to test 4-bit for the pilot but we will likely enable it only after baseline validation week 1.
- SLA: p95 strict, p99 is target but we can accept fallback routing to a cheaper model for p99-only misses during spikes.

Attached: nebulaai_workload_sample.csv (sanitized), nebulaai_telemetry_snapshot.json, nebulaai_security_summary.pdf. We are OK with Redwood running a replay inside a Redwood sandbox under NDA.

Let me know windows for the replay (we'd prefer Wed afternoon PT) and we'll share a signed NDA and SRE contact.

Cheers,
Lisa

Attachments: nebulaai_workload_sample.csv; nebulaai_telemetry_snapshot.json; nebulaai_security_summary.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nebula.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-28T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake — initial snapshot attached

Perfect — thanks for the fast turn. Next steps (summary and owners):

1) NDA & SRE contact (Lisa / Nebula) — once received, we’ll schedule a 4-hr replay window in Redwood sandbox (Owner: Lisa / ops@nebula.ai).
2) Replay & occupancy run (Redwood) — run a 24h synthetic replay using the sanitized sample, produce an occupancy matrix (GPU SKUs, counts, expected p95/p99, and cost delta). ETA: 48 business hours post-replay (Owner: Rishi / Priyom).
3) Pilot configuration proposal — we’ll propose 2 scenarios: conservative reserved (6x A100 + 2x A10 spill) and optimized quantized (estimated 20–30% fewer GPUs). Includes rollout runbook and canary routing plan. ETA: 2 business days after occupancy run. (Owner: Marissa).
4) Contract ask — please confirm target commit length for pilot (3 months preferred vs 8–12 weeks discussed). We’ll include burst credits and an SLA appendix for p95/p99.

Action items: Lisa to send NDA + SRE point of contact and preferred replay window (you mentioned Wed afternoon PT — we have availability 13:00–17:00 PT).

I'll create a mutual action plan and drop a HubSpot task linking the replay artifacts.

Thanks team — we’ll aim to have a first-pass occupancy table ready the week after the replay.

Regards,
Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-link (https://hubspot.redwood.ai/tasks/ND-2027-1147/mutual-action-plan)
